newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia, France to produce rail wheels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia, France to produce rail wheels - paper.

text.p: Serbian railways Zeleznicko Transportno Preduzece (ZTP) Beograd and French firm Valdunes have signed a deal for joint production of rolling stock wheels and axles, the Belgrade newspaper Borba reported on Thursday.

The value of the deal, which will initially cover joint production of wheels for wagons, engines and trains, is expected to reach around 80 million French francs ($15.7 million) in the next five years, the paper said.
Production will later be expanded to include axles for rolling stock.
The contract was signed on Wednesday by ZTP Beograd Management Board President Milomir Minic and Valdunes General Manager Jean-Pierre Auger.
No-one at ZTP Beograd was immediately available for comment.

The deal, if confirmed, was the third signed by Serbian railways with French industry this year, and the first joint venture contract since international sanctions against rump Yugoslavia were lifted in early October.
Rolling stock wheels were not manufactured in Yugoslavia before.

The two sides agreed to set up a Yugoslav-French joint venture firm for machine processing and marketing of wheels within the rolling stock works Zelvoz of Smederevo. The plant is expected to begin operating in September 1997.

Valdunes will over the next year invest a modern production line with an annual capacity for processing 12,000 wheels of various kinds, while ZTP Beograd will provide production and business premises with existing equipment and infrastructure.

"Through the realisation of this project Serbian railways will substantially reduce outflow of hard currency, employ domestic industry and raise its technological level," Minic was quoted by Borba as saying.
-- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305 ($ = 5.104 French Francs)
